specs.scene: A restaurant kitchen pass forms the working surface, order tickets clipped along a rail with several already pinned and one being pinned now by a cook's hand, a delivery invoice held flat under a metal bulldog clip, a wooden produce crate of vegetables pushed into one corner, a handheld barcode scanner resting on its side, a paper reservation book lying open with a pen crossing its spine, a curl of receipt paper unspooling from a printer edge, all crowded to the corners and overlapping at their edges, with bare patches of stainless surface left open between the ticket rail and the crate and beside the reservation book.
specs.source_quote: the reservation fix exposed the inventory mess, the inventory fix exposed the reporting mess

recognisable.why: A restaurant order rail, produce crate and reservation book read instantly as food-service work without any label.

legibility.why: The clutter reads as one dense working-surface texture, though the ticket rail, crate and book each pull the eye separately enough to cost points.

curiosity.why: "One fix exposes three" states a count without naming the three, an open loop the viewer wants closed.

subject.why: The archetype is deliberately scattered, so there is no single anchor beyond a partial hand mid-task.

credible.why: No figure is carried, which this register rewards in full.

stakes.why: The dominant read is the mess itself — tickets, chaos, overlap — closer to a problem shot than a job the viewer is shown taking.

reexpress.why: The mechanism (one fix cascading into three) is a fact the title never states.

specs.scene: A documentary photograph of a glass-fronted corporate office lobby at street level, a consultant in a plain dark suit mid-stride through the revolving door carrying a slim leather laptop bag, the glass and steel surfaces around them left plain and unmarked, morning light crossing the floor, the consultant's face turned slightly away as they walk toward the elevators.
specs.source_quote: if it's that easy, why is Accenture charging billions for it?

recognisable.why: A generic glass office lobby signals corporate consulting broadly but nothing distinctly Accenture without a mark.

legibility.why: One person, one action, one lobby — resolves cleanly at small size.

curiosity.why: "Easy is expensive" is the flat unresolved verdict this register's top quartile runs on.

subject.why: The consultant mid-stride is a single clear human anchor.

credible.why: No figure carried, full credit under this rubric.

stakes.why: The frame proves enterprise demand but doesn't show the viewer a job they could personally take.

reexpress.why: The verdict names a mechanism (easy work still commands a high price) the title's figures don't.

specs.scene: A single small black mini computer sits alone on a plain stainless counter, one coiled ethernet cable running from its back to a compact card reader terminal lying face-down beside it, the counter surface left bare and unmarked on either side, no hands or other objects in frame, the pairing of the two devices the only content in the shot.
specs.source_quote: Accenture's GenAI bookings roughly doubled to five point nine billion dollars

recognisable.why: A mini PC and card reader are familiar objects but don't on their own signal the AI-implementation trade.

legibility.why: Two closely paired devices read as one system, not several separate elements to resolve.

curiosity.why: The gap between a pocket-sized box and a $491 million figure is an unresolved tension the viewer wants explained.

subject.why: A single distinctive object pairing with no person, full credit for object archetype.

credible.why: The figure is a straight division of Accenture's own reported annual bookings into a monthly unit, believable to a skeptical operator.

stakes.why: The cheap, ownable hardware is the literal $100 setup the viewer could buy and run.

reexpress.why: Converts the title's annual $5.9 billion into its smallest honest monthly unit, the exact reexpress pattern the rubric describes.

specs.scene: Close on a pair of hands crouched behind a hotel front desk, one hand holding a small black automation box steady while the other threads a cable toward a nearby reservation printer, the desk's underside and a stretch of blank countertop to the side left clear and unmarked, the hands the only human presence in frame, the action mid-connection.
specs.source_quote: Every source on this business converges on vertical focus

recognisable.why: A hotel front desk is an everyday setting a cold viewer places immediately, though the hands-only crop costs some legibility of the subject.

legibility.why: One action, one small object, one clean crop — a single focal mass at small size.

curiosity.why: "Pick one industry" implies a verdict (which one, and why it matters) without answering it.

subject.why: The installing hands are a clear human anchor mid-action.

stakes.why: This is the job itself — installing the tool at a real business — the clearest opportunity frame of the four.

reexpress.why: The title never mentions vertical focus; this supplies a genuinely new constraint on how to win the business.
